title: Oct 6 Results + Oct 7 Preview: Split Records Are For Losers
summary: We went .500 on Oct 6. Let me be honest—that's not good enough. White Sox redemption tomorrow?

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: .500 Is Mediocrity

You know what a 1-1 record gets you? Absolutely nothing. We're not here to break even, we're here to crush. October 6th was a tale of two games—the Padres came through like champions while the Braves choked harder than a rookie in the World Series. Let's break down this frustrating split.

## The Padres Delivered, The Braves Disappointed

The Padres at 65% confidence? That was the easiest money of the day. San Diego showed up and handled business against Milwaukee like we knew they would. But the Braves? A coin flip at 50% that landed on the wrong side. Atlanta had every opportunity to take care of the Dodgers at home and they folded. This is why you can't trust teams that coast on reputation alone.

Here's the controversial take: **The Braves are overrated in October.** There, I said it. They crumble when the stakes get real.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick Preview: White Sox Chaos Ball

Now let's talk about October 7th, because this is where things get spicy. The model is giving us Cleveland Guardians at Chicago White Sox, and we're backing the **White Sox at 50%**. Yeah, you read that right—another coin flip.

Daniel Espino for Cleveland against Sean Newcomb for Chicago. This isn't a pitching matchup that screams quality—this screams chaos. And in chaos, you take the home dog that everyone's sleeping on.

## Why The White Sox? Let Me Break It Down

The Guardians are going to be overvalued by the public. Everyone sees Cleveland as the "safe" pick, the "smart" pick. But Sean Newcomb at home with nothing to lose? That's dangerous. The White Sox have been written off all season, and that's exactly when teams like this bite back.

**Hot take alert:** Daniel Espino is overhyped. His stuff is electric but his consistency is garbage. One bad inning and this game flips. Meanwhile, Newcomb knows he's fighting for his career—that desperation breeds performance.

Is 50% confidence scary? Absolutely. But fortune favors the bold, and sometimes you have to trust the chaos. The White Sox are live tomorrow, and if you're not riding with us, you're missing out on value.

## Final Word: Redemption Time

A .500 day is unacceptable. We're better than this, the model is better than this, and October 7th is our bounce-back moment. The White Sox pick isn't going to be popular, but that's exactly why it's going to hit.

Stay sharp. Stay hungry. And never settle for mediocrity.

**– Rico**
